1
00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.460
Elena compares a personally owned whole life policy with coverage offered

2
00:00:04.460 --> 00:00:09.260
through work. Individual and group describe how coverage is arranged.

3
00:00:10.200 --> 00:00:14.100
Temporary and permanent describe the intended protection pattern.

4
00:00:14.920 --> 00:00:19.700
Participating and nonparticipating describe whether the contract provides for

5
00:00:19.700 --> 00:00:24.740
policy dividends. Fixed and variable describe important differences

6
00:00:24.740 --> 00:00:27.200
in guarantees and investment risk.

7
00:00:28.140 --> 00:00:30.020
These labels answer different questions.

8
00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:36.200
One policy can be individual, permanent, participating and fixed

9
00:00:36.200 --> 00:00:37.660
at the same time.

10
00:00:38.440 --> 00:00:43.600
Ordinary life is a broad individual-life category; do not assume

11
00:00:43.600 --> 00:00:47.820
that every use of the word ordinary means one particular premium

12
00:00:47.820 --> 00:00:52.278
schedule. A participating life policy may pay dividends,

13
00:00:52.898 --> 00:00:56.458
but those dividends are not guaranteed merely because the policy

14
00:00:56.458 --> 00:01:01.918
participates. A fixed design provides the guarantees stated in its contract;

15
00:01:02.838 --> 00:01:07.878
the label does not erase charges, funding requirements or exclusions.

16
00:01:08.498 --> 00:01:13.518
Variable life uses investment options whose results can affect values

17
00:01:13.518 --> 00:01:15.698
and benefits within the policy's terms.

18
00:01:16.038 --> 00:01:19.098
The owner bears the specified investment risk.

19
00:01:19.618 --> 00:01:23.398
Variable products also involve securities requirements in addition to

20
00:01:23.398 --> 00:01:27.918
insurance authority. Before discussing price, know what protection,

21
00:01:28.418 --> 00:01:32.598
guarantees, charges and risks are actually being compared.

22
00:01:33.498 --> 00:01:36.758
Similar labels do not prove identical contracts.

23
00:01:37.812 --> 00:01:42.392
The insurer studies mortality: the expected pattern of deaths in the

24
00:01:42.392 --> 00:01:47.012
insured group. Interest assumptions reflect earnings on funds held before

25
00:01:47.012 --> 00:01:52.412
benefits are paid. Expenses include the costs of acquiring, administering

26
00:01:53.232 --> 00:01:56.492
and servicing the business, with appropriate pricing provisions.

27
00:01:57.532 --> 00:02:01.932
Holding other assumptions constant, higher expected mortality tends to

28
00:02:01.932 --> 00:02:03.812
increase the cost of death protection.

29
00:02:04.732 --> 00:02:08.372
Higher assumed interest can reduce the amount that must be collected

30
00:02:08.372 --> 00:02:10.652
now for the same future benefit.

31
00:02:11.352 --> 00:02:14.112
Greater expense needs increase the gross price.

32
00:02:14.872 --> 00:02:19.352
These are pricing relationships, not promises that the premium on an

33
00:02:19.352 --> 00:02:23.252
existing policy changes whenever market conditions move.

34
00:02:24.222 --> 00:02:26.642
Use a simplified one-year example.

35
00:02:27.522 --> 00:02:31.652
Assume a two-in-one-thousand chance of death and a one hundred thousand

36
00:02:31.652 --> 00:02:33.842
dollar benefit paid at year end.

37
00:02:34.422 --> 00:02:38.142
The expected benefit cost is two hundred dollars per policy before

38
00:02:38.142 --> 00:02:43.602
expenses and discounting. If the explicitly assumed interest rate is five

39
00:02:43.602 --> 00:02:48.262
percent, dividing two hundred by one point zero five gives a

40
00:02:48.262 --> 00:02:51.702
present value of about one hundred ninety dollars and forty-eight cents.

41
00:02:52.532 --> 00:02:56.262
This illustrates a net single premium under the stated assumptions.

42
00:02:57.242 --> 00:03:01.282
Real life pricing uses fuller mortality and timing data.

43
00:03:02.092 --> 00:03:06.032
It is not simply the face amount divided by a guessed

44
00:03:06.032 --> 00:03:09.966
lifespan. A net single premium is paid once in the simplified

45
00:03:09.966 --> 00:03:15.266
model. A net level annual premium spreads funding over the assumed

46
00:03:15.266 --> 00:03:19.846
premium-paying period while accounting for timing, interest and the

47
00:03:19.846 --> 00:03:22.146
possibility that premiums stop at death.

48
00:03:22.906 --> 00:03:27.966
The gross annual premium adds the applicable expense and other pricing

49
00:03:27.966 --> 00:03:31.606
provisions. Do not compare a net single amount with a gross

50
00:03:31.606 --> 00:03:35.146
annual quote as if they described the same payment.

51
00:03:35.596 --> 00:03:40.166
The insurer's actual quoted premium reflects the selected product, risk

52
00:03:40.526 --> 00:03:44.806
classification, benefit, guarantees and payment arrangement.

53
00:03:45.606 --> 00:03:49.126
A teaching calculation explains a principle; it does not replace an

54
00:03:49.126 --> 00:03:53.916
insurer's approved quote. Elena can pay four hundred eighty dollars annually

55
00:03:53.916 --> 00:03:58.136
or forty-two dollars monthly for the stated coverage.

56
00:03:59.296 --> 00:04:04.556
Twelve monthly payments total five hundred four dollars, which is twenty-four

57
00:04:04.556 --> 00:04:06.376
dollars more per year.

58
00:04:07.216 --> 00:04:11.596
Payment mode means frequency, such as annual,

59
00:04:12.416 --> 00:04:15.236
semiannual, quarterly or monthly.

60
00:04:15.956 --> 00:04:20.836
The monthly amount is not necessarily the annual premium divided by

61
00:04:20.836 --> 00:04:25.616
twelve. Compare the total cost as well as affordability and the

62
00:04:25.616 --> 00:04:30.076
contract's payment conditions. Keep the final distinctions clear:

63
00:04:30.976 --> 00:04:35.456
the product describes the coverage, pricing assumptions help determine its

64
00:04:35.456 --> 00:04:40.836
cost, and payment mode describes the schedule
on which premiums are collected.

1
00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.840
Marcus wants protection while his children are financially dependent.

2
00:00:05.080 --> 00:00:08.820
A term policy covers a specified period if the contract stays

3
00:00:08.820 --> 00:00:12.900
in force. Ordinary term generally has no cash accumulation.

4
00:00:13.780 --> 00:00:17.660
Ask four separate questions: how long protection lasts, how the death

5
00:00:17.660 --> 00:00:21.860
benefit changes, how long the premium is guaranteed, and what rights

6
00:00:21.860 --> 00:00:26.740
exist afterward. A level benefit does not by itself promise a

7
00:00:26.740 --> 00:00:29.960
level premium forever. Read the schedules.

8
00:00:30.980 --> 00:00:34.840
Maryland also requires clear language about whether a death on the

9
00:00:34.840 --> 00:00:36.640
term's expiry date is covered.

10
00:00:37.740 --> 00:00:41.720
A single word such as term cannot settle all those questions.

11
00:00:42.402 --> 00:00:46.302
A stated twenty-year policy keeps a five hundred thousand dollar death

12
00:00:46.302 --> 00:00:50.322
benefit and a guaranteed annual premium of six hundred dollars during

13
00:00:50.322 --> 00:00:54.202
that period. The benefit and premium are both level under these

14
00:00:54.202 --> 00:00:58.462
particular terms. If the contract permits renewal afterward at a higher

15
00:00:58.462 --> 00:01:02.622
scheduled rate, that does not extend the original six hundred dollar

16
00:01:02.622 --> 00:01:07.642
guarantee. Annual renewable term uses one-year periods and

17
00:01:07.642 --> 00:01:11.302
commonly increases its renewal premium as the insured ages.

18
00:01:11.762 --> 00:01:15.582
A lower starting premium should be compared with future costs and

19
00:01:15.582 --> 00:01:18.802
the length of the need, not treated as the price for

20
00:01:18.802 --> 00:01:23.648
every future year. A renewable provision gives the owner the stated

21
00:01:23.648 --> 00:01:28.528
right to continue term coverage without new evidence of insurability.

22
00:01:29.548 --> 00:01:34.368
The right still has conditions, such as age limits, premium payment

23
00:01:34.828 --> 00:01:36.848
and the available renewal period.

24
00:01:38.048 --> 00:01:42.188
It does not guarantee the old premium or permit renewal after

25
00:01:42.188 --> 00:01:47.208
every stated limit. Maryland requires the actual renewal premiums to

26
00:01:47.208 --> 00:01:49.948
appear in an individual renewable term policy.

27
00:01:50.768 --> 00:01:55.268
Its rule has a separate provision for wholesale and group coverage.

28
00:01:56.488 --> 00:02:01.228
For Marcus, worsening health makes an available renewal right valuable,

29
00:02:02.208 --> 00:02:06.308
but he must still consider the renewal price and exercise the

30
00:02:06.308 --> 00:02:11.146
right on time. A conversion provision allows an eligible owner to

31
00:02:11.146 --> 00:02:16.406
exchange term coverage for an available permanent policy without new evidence

32
00:02:16.406 --> 00:02:19.506
of insurability, within the stated limits.

33
00:02:20.166 --> 00:02:23.286
Conversion is different from renewing another term period.

34
00:02:24.006 --> 00:02:28.126
Marcus develops a medical condition but still has an available conversion

35
00:02:28.126 --> 00:02:33.086
right. He should check the deadline, eligible permanent products,

36
00:02:33.786 --> 00:02:36.066
allowed amount and premium basis.

37
00:02:36.946 --> 00:02:41.626
The new premium is commonly based on attained age, meaning his

38
00:02:41.626 --> 00:02:44.866
age at conversion, under the contract's rules.

39
00:02:45.786 --> 00:02:49.026
No new health evidence does not mean no new premium.

40
00:02:50.086 --> 00:02:53.886
Missing the conversion window can remove that particular right.

41
00:02:54.744 --> 00:03:00.084
A decreasing term design reduces its death benefit according to

42
00:03:00.084 --> 00:03:04.384
a schedule, often to address a declining obligation.

43
00:03:05.564 --> 00:03:10.584
Its premium does not necessarily decrease; many designs keep it

44
00:03:10.584 --> 00:03:15.644
level. In an increasing term design, the benefit grows

45
00:03:15.644 --> 00:03:19.444
under the stated formula or schedule.

46
00:03:19.444 --> 00:03:24.644
These labels concern the benefit, not a cash-value

47
00:03:24.644 --> 00:03:27.514
account. Suppose a teaching

48
00:03:27.514 --> 00:03:32.821
policy starts at one hundred thousand dollars and adds five thousand

49
00:03:32.821 --> 00:03:35.134
dollars at each anniversary.

50
00:03:36.334 --> 00:03:41.234
After two increases, its benefit is one hundred ten thousand dollars.

51
00:03:41.234 --> 00:03:46.594
Use the stated formula rather than assuming every increasing

52
00:03:46.594 --> 00:03:49.014
design compounds a percentage.

53
00:03:50.088 --> 00:03:54.608
Return-of-premium term adds a contractual refund feature if the insured

54
00:03:54.608 --> 00:03:58.528
survives the stated period and the required conditions are met.

55
00:03:58.888 --> 00:04:03.888
It commonly costs more than otherwise comparable term without that feature.

56
00:04:04.308 --> 00:04:07.348
Do not promise a full refund after any early cancellation or

57
00:04:07.348 --> 00:04:09.268
assume every rider charge is included.

58
00:04:09.688 --> 00:04:13.568
In a simplified example, one thousand dollars of qualifying annual premiums

59
00:04:13.568 --> 00:04:16.648
paid for twenty years totals twenty thousand dollars.

60
00:04:17.328 --> 00:04:20.828
That arithmetic does not create a guaranteed investment return.

61
00:04:21.308 --> 00:04:25.968
Compare the protection, total cost, refund conditions and alternatives.

62
00:04:27.128 --> 00:04:31.108
The policy should fit the client's need and sustainable budget.

1
00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.000
Marcus can no longer afford the continuing premiums on his whole

2
00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:08.100
life policy. Before he gives it up, he reviews its nonforfeiture

3
00:00:08.100 --> 00:00:12.400
choices. These choices use the value already built under the policy

4
00:00:12.400 --> 00:00:14.060
when premium payments stop.

5
00:00:14.540 --> 00:00:19.340
The familiar alternatives are taking available cash, using value for extended

6
00:00:19.340 --> 00:00:23.940
term insurance, or keeping a smaller amount of paid-up permanent insurance.

7
00:00:24.580 --> 00:00:25.900
They preserve different things.

8
00:00:25.900 --> 00:00:30.920
A no-cash-value term policy does not suddenly acquire those values because

9
00:00:30.920 --> 00:00:32.140
its premium is missed.

10
00:00:32.840 --> 00:00:36.500
Start with the actual policy, current values and any outstanding debt.

11
00:00:37.020 --> 00:00:39.980
Then compare what protection would remain under each available choice.

12
00:00:40.523 --> 00:00:43.903
Cash surrender pays the available surrender amount to the owner and

13
00:00:43.903 --> 00:00:45.783
ends the surrendered policy's protection.

14
00:00:46.243 --> 00:00:47.803
It is not an advance death claim.

15
00:00:48.423 --> 00:00:52.963
Suppose the insurer's statement shows twelve thousand dollars available

16
00:00:52.963 --> 00:00:56.763
before a separately listed two thousand dollar policy debt, with no

17
00:00:56.763 --> 00:01:00.783
other adjustment. The net cash payment is ten thousand dollars.

18
00:01:01.443 --> 00:01:05.143
If the quoted amount already includes that debt, do not deduct

19
00:01:05.143 --> 00:01:09.543
it again. Surrender can also have tax consequences, addressed in the

20
00:01:09.543 --> 00:01:13.363
tax lessons. The owner should understand the lost death protection before

21
00:01:13.363 --> 00:01:17.243
signing. A later change of mind does not create an automatic

22
00:01:17.243 --> 00:01:19.923
right to reinstate a cash-surrendered policy.

23
00:01:20.525 --> 00:01:25.625
Under the simplified extended-term choice, the available value buys term

24
00:01:25.625 --> 00:01:30.425
protection at the original face amount
for as long as that value purchases.

26
00:01:31.353 --> 00:01:34.913
No further premiums are required for that purchased period.

27
00:01:36.013 --> 00:01:39.253
Assume a debt-free policy with a one hundred thousand dollar face

28
00:01:39.253 --> 00:01:43.513
amount. Its actual table offers one hundred thousand dollars of extended

29
00:01:43.513 --> 00:01:44.853
term for eight years.

30
00:01:45.633 --> 00:01:48.953
A covered death in year seven falls within that period.

31
00:01:49.873 --> 00:01:51.533
Death in year nine does not.

32
00:01:52.333 --> 00:01:56.833
Eight years comes from this hypothetical table, not a universal formula.

33
00:01:57.653 --> 00:02:01.433
Debt, additions and the contract can affect the actual benefit and

34
00:02:01.433 --> 00:02:06.895
duration. Reduced paid-up insurance uses available value

35
00:02:06.895 --> 00:02:11.595
to continue a smaller amount of permanent life protection with no

36
00:02:11.595 --> 00:02:15.695
further required premiums for that reduced base benefit.

37
00:02:16.195 --> 00:02:21.875
Assume the same policy offers thirty-two thousand dollars of reduced paid-up

38
00:02:21.875 --> 00:02:25.445
whole life. The family gives up part of the former one

39
00:02:25.445 --> 00:02:29.815
hundred thousand dollar amount but keeps the smaller permanent benefit.

40
00:02:29.815 --> 00:02:34.235
This is different from paying the final scheduled premium on a

41
00:02:34.235 --> 00:02:38.115
limited-pay contract and keeping its original promised amount.

42
00:02:39.195 --> 00:02:43.595
It is also different from purchasing paid-up additions with a dividend.

43
00:02:44.595 --> 00:02:49.175
Review whether riders continue and how debt affects the actual option.

44
00:02:49.813 --> 00:02:54.433
Maryland's standard provision for these choices gives the specified election

45
00:02:54.433 --> 00:02:58.513
opportunity within sixty days after the due date of the premium

46
00:02:58.513 --> 00:03:03.213
in default. If the entitled person does not choose another available

47
00:03:03.213 --> 00:03:08.333
option in that period, the policy's specified paid-up benefit takes effect.

48
00:03:09.053 --> 00:03:13.393
Do not automatically name extended term as the required default for

49
00:03:13.393 --> 00:03:18.513
every Maryland policy. Read the policy's own provision and the statute's

50
00:03:18.513 --> 00:03:23.653
applicability rules. The standard statute also distinguishes paid-up

51
00:03:23.653 --> 00:03:28.913
benefit eligibility from ordinary and industrial cash-surrender minimums.

52
00:03:29.593 --> 00:03:32.813
A more favorable contract may provide value earlier.

53
00:03:33.753 --> 00:03:37.613
Contact the insurer promptly while the choice remains available.

54
00:03:38.215 --> 00:03:40.375
Marcus compares the three hypothetical offers.

55
00:03:41.175 --> 00:03:44.115
If his stated priority is ten thousand dollars of immediate net

56
00:03:44.115 --> 00:03:48.515
cash and ending this protection, cash surrender matches that objective.

57
00:03:49.475 --> 00:03:52.015
If he wants the stated one hundred thousand dollar benefit for

58
00:03:52.015 --> 00:03:56.195
the next eight years without more premiums, extended term matches it.

59
00:03:56.815 --> 00:04:01.115
If he wants some permanent protection without continuing premiums, the

60
00:04:01.115 --> 00:04:04.915
thirty-two thousand dollar reduced paid-up option matches that goal.

61
00:04:04.915 --> 00:04:10.015
Those are exam comparisons using supplied facts, not a recommendation

62
00:04:10.015 --> 00:04:14.915
for every family. Review current protection needs, remaining resources,

63
00:04:15.375 --> 00:04:19.695
tax effects and the actual written values
before an owner makes a real decision.
